subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should dashboard widget write-back proceed only with SQLite/plugin-KV storage and reviewed sandbox capability semantics, or may maintainers approve a named JSON-state and write-back exception for this dashboard stack?
rationale: The feature is useful and aligned with dashboard ergonomics, but it changes persisted runtime state and the sandbox write boundary; automation should not choose the permanent storage and security model.

options.title: Require storage and security repair
options.body: Proceed with the capability after moving state into plugin KV/shared SQLite or another approved SQLite owner, defining the bridge contract, and adding adversarial/live proof.

options.title: Approve a named exception
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept JSON sidecar state and the proposed write-back boundary as intentional product debt before the candidate PR continues.

options.title: Defer behind dashboard base
options.body: Keep the issue open under the roadmap until the prerequisite dashboard stack lands or is rejected, then re-review the write-back delta.

recommendation.title: Require storage and security repair
recommendation.body: Proceed with the capability after moving state into plugin KV/shared SQLite or another approved SQLite owner, defining the bridge contract, and adding adversarial/live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-main history signal for the Control UI plugin-tab seam and adjacent plugin storage precedent this work extends.
